source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting results that contradict the hypothesis in a psychology research report

1. Start with the research records.
2.
completion:
Discard any information, tables, graphs, and images of results that are inconsistent with the hypothesis.
3. Prepare a manuscript. 

It appears psychology papers are not taught in the same way other sciences are when conducting experimental research.  It would be reasonable to expect them to make good records including those observations and interpretations that run contrary to the hypothesis (that is, record everything).  But I will bet the vast majority of PhD candidates in psychology never take a record keeping class, and thus do not know how to keep accurate records under their set of circumstances.  I don't know how far along in the pipeline the problem of inaccurate record keeping starts, but it certainly propagates in the published literature.  A good record keeping class would not be trivial, but if it were, it would teach that the purpose of record keeping is to record what is observed in a single pass, and not start over again until that is complete.
